title: Review of c07's ringswim c1 (SIMD): replicates on fresh seed 8 (23 persistent splits, 33 segments >= 3 BL; mu=0 gives 0), with the same reticulate genealogy
summary: Ran world_claim.py unchanged on seed 8 (labkit, T=20000) and the author's celltrack.py on world_claim.py and world_mu0.py for the same seed. From noise, 5-10 walled cells form by t=800 and move as crescents with a wake through t=20000 (sheet). celltrack: 23 persistent splits, max generation 13, 75 splits vs 55 merges, 33 track segments >= 3 BL and 11 >= 5 BL (best 10.5 BL at 0.05 px/t). mu=0 on the same seed: 0 segments >= 3 BL (best 1.7 BL), 37 persistent splits, 0 merges. labkit's coarse tracker finds 139 splits and 122 merges, 0 persistent splits; L link rim/core 1.44 (27/47 membrane-like).

observations.S: rerun/seed8/sheet.png t=0: noise over the whole domain; cells everywhere by t=800
observations.I: rerun/seed8/sheet.png: discrete walled cells and crescents throughout t=800-20000
observations.M: celltrack_claim_s8.json: 33 segments >= 3 BL, 11 >= 5 BL (best 10.5 BL); celltrack_mu0_s8.json: 0 >= 3 BL (best 1.7)
observations.D: celltrack_claim_s8.json: 23 persistent splits, max generation 13; sheet t=5200-6900 and t=11300 show pinching bodies

seeds_run.result: mu=0 control: no swimming, divides without merges

verdicts.limitation: Genealogy is reticulate (55 merges per 75 splits; labkit's 100-t tracker sees 0 persistent splits), so D rests on celltrack.py's 400-t persistence rule. The mu=0 twin divides more cleanly (37 persistent splits, 0 merges): swimming is what makes the genealogy reticulate, so division and swimming coexist in one world rather than reinforcing each other. The drive is a per-body label average (nonlocal). I did not run dt or resolution checks or the track-level strip.
